correctness.rationale: A fresh independently implemented C++ exact base-three enumerator traversed all 3^12=531441 states from the actual graph edge list, verified F^9=F^6 for each state, and reconstructed the 7-column period1/period3 entrance table and 60 extremal states. A separate independent Python phase-condition enumerator found 145200 3-periodic states, 48400 temporal orbits, and used the complete 120 automorphisms to recover 473 classes with size spectrum {5:2,20:4,30:11,40:10,60:99,120:347}. These enumerations cover the COMPLETE finite space, not a sample. The all-rotating successor-neighbor phase characterization and full automorphism order bound were checked in the mathematical package.

evidence: General circulation and maximum-cycle-density results explain fixation vs persistent activity for triangulated graphs, without the exact F^9=F^6 stopping-time identity or labelled basin multiplicities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader qualitative dynamical theorems do not entail the numerical census without a distinct enumeration or graph-specific combinatorics.

value.rationale: The icosahedron is a canonical minimal 5-regular Platonic graph. Exact transient cutoffs, cycle basins, and full spatial symmetry quotient give natural graph-specific nonlinear dynamical invariants; all 60 longest transient states forming one geometric orbit is a meaningful structural feature beyond qualitative periodicity.

limitations: Only this 12-vertex, 30-edge labelled icosahedral graph, exact 3-state threshold-one synchronous rule.
Full-state exact enumeration proves only this finite-graph theorem, not an arbitrary-graph result.
An unindexed preexisting icosahedral 3-coloring enumeration or phase-difference table could already contain matching numbers.
Exact all-state counts are an object-specific classification and do not generalize to other polyhedral graphs.
